title: tsdk: union pattern-match helpers + Zod/JSON-Schema shorthand generators for streamed and chunked shapes
creator: Marco Chen
description:
Goal: ship small, ergonomically friendly helpers and codegen changes in the TypeScript SDK to make it trivial for client code to consume structured output from models that produce discriminated unions and for streaming responses that may arrive as chunked partial objects. This ticket covers: (1) a pattern-match helper (matchUnion) that narrows union members at runtime via discriminator keys, (2) a lightweight Zod/JSON-Schema generation helper that emits concise validators for generated types (including union unions), and (3) streaming-safe shape hinting so that partial chunks can be reassembled and validated incrementally.

Why: teams keep hand-rolling repetitive narrowers and validators for model outputs. Streaming responses add complexity because partial chunks may arrive without the discriminator present until later. A small, well-documented set of helpers plus codegen hooks will reduce bugs, speed adoption, and allow consistent validation for quality monitoring.

Scope: TypeScript SDK only. No changes to Python/Go in this ticket (follow-ups planned). Backwards-compatible API additions only. Codegen changes limited to adding optional flags that opt-in consumers to the new helpers.

Out-of-scope: heavy-weight schema bundles or runtime-only deps that increase bundle size by >15%. Full TypeScript AST rework (future ticket).
acceptance_criteria: matchUnion exported from @redwood/tsdk provides a zero-dependency narrow() helper that accepts a discriminator key and a mapping of handlers and returns an exhaustive-checked result at compile time.
Codegen emits an optional --zod-shorthand flag that generates Zod schemas next to generated types for simple objects, unions, and arrays (no circular refs in this MVP).

An incremental validator API (validateChunk) can accept partial JSON chunks plus a shape-hint and return either (a) 'incomplete' with a merge token, (b) 'valid' with typed value, or (c) 'validation_error' with zod-style issues.

Examples folder includes two runnable examples: examples/union-patterns.ts and examples/streamed-validation.ts demonstrating typical client usage with streaming SSE/websocket and server-simulated chunk order reassembly.
Unit tests cover 95% of new helpers and codegen output comparisons (golden files), integration test runs against a deterministic local model stub.
Documentation page created at /docs/tsdk/struct-output with usage, migration notes, and bundle-size table.
implementation_notes: Planned approach: 1) matchUnion: implement as (value, mapping) => mapping[value[discriminator]] with TypeScript mapped types to ensure exhaustiveness. Include fallback handler type for unknown variants. 2) Zod shorthand: a minimal generator that emits zod.object/array/union calls with simple .optional/.nullable mapping, skipping deep transforms. Keep output opt-in via --zod-shorthand to avoid increasing bundle size for consumers who don't use zod. 3) Streaming hints: introduce per-message metadata (shapeHint: "root"|"partial-object"|"array-chunk" and optional path) in the client-side reassembler; validateChunk will run Zod validators only when discriminator and required fields are present, otherwise return an opaque merge token. 4) CLI/codegen changes: add flags in the existing tsdk generator; generated files live alongside types in generated/schemas/*.ts. 5) Backwards compatibility: generated types unchanged unless --zod-shorthand is enabled. 6) Performance: avoid heavy runtime helpers; zod imports only when user opts in. 7) Expose lightweight runtime guards for popular patterns (isVariantX).
testing_notes:
- Unit tests for matchUnion behavior (exhaustive and fallback paths), for zod-shorthand generated code (compare to golden zod files), and for validateChunk paths (incomplete->merge token, valid, invalid).
- Integration: run examples against local model-stub that emits chunk reorder scenarios (missing discriminator in first chunk).
- Bench: measure bundle size impact when --zod-shorthand enabled vs disabled; target <12% increase when enabled.
- E2E: run example with Redwood Console eval pipeline to ensure telemetry for validation failures is recorded.
- CI: add golden-update script and fixture runner.
blockers: Decision on whether to support circular schemas in next quarter
